svg.title: What committing first is worth, as a number
svg.desc: In a simultaneous game neither side sees the other's choice, so the solution is a mixed strategy that is hard to exploit. In a leader-follower game the leader commits to a policy first and the follower observes it before responding, which sounds like a disadvantage but is often worth more, because a credible commitment shapes what the follower will do. Subtracting the leader's value in the simultaneous solution from the leader's value in the leader-follower solution gives the price of committing early, as a single figure the planner can weigh.
svg.text: The answer is a mixed strategy: hard to exploit, and it
assumes your opponent never learns your policy.
The leader commits, and is seen doing it
Sounds worse. Often is not — a credible commitment
changes what the follower finds worth doing.
This matches the real situation: a handler plans before an operative acts.
one number, weighable against the cost of committing
Choosing the equilibrium concept is a modelling decision, not a maths one.
Ask who actually moves first, then pick the solver that matches.
